newsitem.title: BELGIUM: France's Chirac fears U.S. pressure over Boeing.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac fears U.S. pressure over Boeing.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Thursday he fully backed the European Commission's plans to block the merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas, but he was worried about U.S. pressure on individual EU governments.
"We back the Commission without reservation," Chirac told a news conference.
He added: "I don't fear for the Commission. The problem is more about the position of the (EU) states which clearly risk being submitted to a strong psychological pressure."

U.S. President Bill Clinton said earlier on Thursday that he was concerned about the EU's objections to the $14 billion merger. Clinton said, however, that the deal should not take the two partners into a "trade war".
Chirac was speaking after a meeting with Commission President Jacques Santer on a number of issues.
The Commission is expected to block the merger at its regular meeting on Wednesday on the grounds that it would harm fair competition in Europe unless Boeing meets its concerns.
